sections.title: Paywall Body — every setting
sections.summary: The paywall's words — the headline and subtitle (with full typography) and the feature-benefit bullet list, including each bullet's box style, padding, and per-bullet title / subtitle / icon styling. This guide documents every setting of the Paywall Body block, grouped by area. Each setting matches a real control in the screen editor.

sections.title: Paywall Body section
sections.summary: The Paywall Body is the persuasion area above the plan cards, where you write the title, subtitle, and feature bullets that explain why the offer is worth paying for. Keep the title to one clear benefit and use the bullets for proof like guarantees and what's included, since this copy is what lifts conversion before the visitor ever looks at the price. Edit it on any paywall screen, ideally after connecting Stripe so the benefits you promise match the plans on sale.

sections.title: Where it appears
sections.summary: Covered screen types: Paywall.

sections.title: Style the bullet icons
sections.summary: Styles the small icon or image on each bullet: how it sits in its box (fit shows the whole image, fill crops it to cover), how rounded the corners are, and the spacing around it, applied to all bullets at once. Keep icon size and shape consistent so the checklist looks tidy. The theme defaults are a safe start.

sections.title: Style the bullet subtitles
sections.summary: Styles the secondary line under each bullet title: font, size, weight, color, alignment, and spacing, applied to all bullets at once. Keep it smaller and lighter than the bullet title so the benefit itself stays the focus. Leave the theme defaults unless the text is hard to read.

sections.title: Style the bullet titles
sections.summary: Styles the main line of every feature bullet: font, size, weight, color, alignment, and spacing, applied to all bullets at once. Keep bullet titles bold and easy to read so each benefit lands at a glance. The theme defaults usually work, so change them only if a benefit is hard to read.

sections.title: Benefit checklist
sections.summary: The list of benefits below the subtitle, your main proof the offer is worth paying for. Add one bullet per concrete benefit (what's included, guarantees, results), each with a title, optional subtitle, and icon, and drag to reorder. Aim for 3 to 5 punchy bullets, since too many dilute the message. Use 'Add Bullet' to create one, or clone an existing bullet to keep the styling consistent.

sections.title: Space inside each bullet
sections.summary: Sets the breathing room inside each bullet, between its text or icon and the bullet's edge, adjustable on the top, bottom, left, and right. Increase it if bullets feel cramped, decrease it to fit more on screen. The theme default is usually fine, so tweak only if the spacing looks off in preview.

sections.title: Style the feature bullets
sections.summary: Sets the background color, border, and corner rounding applied to every bullet in the list at once. Use a subtle card background or border only if you want the bullets to read as a grouped card; otherwise the theme defaults look cleanest. Styling once keeps all bullets consistent.

sections.title: Space around the bullet list
sections.summary: Sets the space around the whole list of bullets, separating it from the subtitle above and the plans below. (Bullet padding spaces the inside of one bullet; this spaces the entire group.) Add space if the list feels jammed against the title or the plan cards; the theme default is a safe start.

sections.title: Style the paywall subtitle
sections.summary: Styles the subtitle line: font, size, weight, color, alignment, and the spacing around it. Keep it smaller and lighter than the headline so the main benefit stays dominant. Leave the theme defaults unless the subtitle is hard to read against your background.

sections.title: Supporting subtitle
sections.summary: The supporting line just under the headline. Use it to back up the promise with a reason to believe or a specific outcome (e.g. 'Cancel anytime, no questions asked'). You can drop in @variables to reference the user's earlier answers for a personal touch. Turn it off to hide the subtitle.

sections.title: Style the paywall headline
sections.summary: Styles the headline: font, size, weight, color, alignment, and the spacing around it. Keep it large and high-contrast so the main benefit is the first thing the eye lands on. Most users can leave the theme defaults; change them only if the title is hard to read against your background.

sections.title: Paywall headline
sections.summary: The big headline at the top of the paywall, your one shot to state your strongest benefit in a few words (e.g. 'Reach your goal in 4 weeks'). You can insert @variables like @{user.name} to echo answers the user gave earlier, which makes the offer feel personal and lifts conversion. Turn it off to hide the headline entirely.

nodes.label: Intro

translations.en: The paywall's words — the headline and subtitle (with full typography) and the feature-benefit bullet list, including each bullet's box style, padding, and per-bullet title / subtitle / icon styling. This guide documents every setting of the Paywall Body block, grouped by area. Each setting matches a real control in the screen editor.

nodes.label: Paywall Body in the editor

en.name: The screen editor with the Paywall Body section highlighted.

nodes.label: Context caption

translations.en: Open the Paywall Body section in the screen editor to configure its settings.

nodes.label: Group: Headline & subtitle
Headline & subtitle · Paywall headline

translations.en: The big headline at the top of the paywall, your one shot to state your strongest benefit in a few words (e.g. 'Reach your goal in 4 weeks'). You can insert @variables like @{user.name} to echo answers the user gave earlier, which makes the offer feel personal and lifts conversion. Turn it off to hide the headline entirely.

nodes.label: Paywall headline

en.name: Where to find “Paywall headline” in the editor.

nodes.label: Headline & subtitle · Style the paywall headline

translations.en: Styles the headline: font, size, weight, color, alignment, and the spacing around it. Keep it large and high-contrast so the main benefit is the first thing the eye lands on. Most users can leave the theme defaults; change them only if the title is hard to read against your background.

nodes.label: Style the paywall headline

en.name: Where to find “Style the paywall headline” in the editor.

nodes.label: Style the paywall headline · Text background color

translations.en: An optional fill drawn behind the paywall headline text (a highlight pill). Off unless you set it; leave empty for plain text on the screen background.

nodes.label: Style the paywall headline · Font family

translations.en: The typeface of the paywall headline.

nodes.label: Style the paywall headline · Line height

translations.en: Vertical spacing between lines of text — raise it to give multi-line text more breathing room.

nodes.label: Style the paywall headline · Font size

translations.en: Text size of the paywall headline in pixels.

nodes.label: Style the paywall headline · Font weight

translations.en: How bold the text is, from Thin through Bold to Black.

nodes.label: Style the paywall headline · Text color

translations.en: The color of the paywall headline text. Keep enough contrast with the background that it stays readable.

nodes.label: Style the paywall headline · Text align

translations.en: Horizontal alignment of the text: start (left), center, or end (right).

nodes.label: Style the paywall headline · Strikethrough color

translations.en: Color of a line-through decoration when the text is struck out (for example, an old price).

nodes.label: Style the paywall headline · Background opacity

translations.en: How see-through the text background fill is, from 0% (invisible) to 100% (solid). Only matters when a background color is set.

nodes.label: Style the paywall headline · Background radius

translations.en: Corner rounding (px) of the text background fill; higher is softer.

nodes.label: Headline & subtitle · Supporting subtitle

translations.en: The supporting line just under the headline. Use it to back up the promise with a reason to believe or a specific outcome (e.g. 'Cancel anytime, no questions asked'). You can drop in @variables to reference the user's earlier answers for a personal touch. Turn it off to hide the subtitle.

translations.en: Styles the subtitle line: font, size, weight, color, alignment, and the spacing around it. Keep it smaller and lighter than the headline so the main benefit stays dominant. Leave the theme defaults unless the subtitle is hard to read against your background.

nodes.label: Group: Feature bullets
Feature bullets · Benefit checklist

translations.en: The list of benefits below the subtitle, your main proof the offer is worth paying for. Add one bullet per concrete benefit (what's included, guarantees, results), each with a title, optional subtitle, and icon, and drag to reorder. Aim for 3 to 5 punchy bullets, since too many dilute the message. Use 'Add Bullet' to create one, or clone an existing bullet to keep the styling consistent.

nodes.label: Benefit checklist

en.name: Where to find “Benefit checklist” in the editor.

nodes.label: Feature bullets · Style the feature bullets

translations.en: Sets the background color, border, and corner rounding applied to every bullet in the list at once. Use a subtle card background or border only if you want the bullets to read as a grouped card; otherwise the theme defaults look cleanest. Styling once keeps all bullets consistent.

nodes.label: Style the feature bullets

en.name: Where to find “Style the feature bullets” in the editor.

nodes.label: Style the feature bullets · Bullet background color

translations.en: Fill behind each feature bullet row. Leave empty for plain bullets on the screen background, or set a subtle tint to group each benefit into its own chip.

nodes.label: Style the feature bullets · Bullet border width

translations.en: Thickness (px) of the outline around each bullet; 0 hides it.

nodes.label: Style the feature bullets · Bullet border color

translations.en: Color of that outline — only visible once the border width is above 0.

nodes.label: Style the feature bullets · Bullet corner radius

translations.en: How rounded each bullet box corner is (px); higher is softer, for pill-shaped benefit chips.

nodes.label: Feature bullets · Space inside each bullet

translations.en: Sets the breathing room inside each bullet, between its text or icon and the bullet's edge, adjustable on the top, bottom, left, and right. Increase it if bullets feel cramped, decrease it to fit more on screen. The theme default is usually fine, so tweak only if the spacing looks off in preview.

nodes.label: Space inside each bullet

en.name: Where to find “Space inside each bullet” in the editor.

nodes.label: Feature bullets · Space around the bullet list

translations.en: Sets the space around the whole list of bullets, separating it from the subtitle above and the plans below. (Bullet padding spaces the inside of one bullet; this spaces the entire group.) Add space if the list feels jammed against the title or the plan cards; the theme default is a safe start.

nodes.label: Space around the bullet list

en.name: Where to find “Space around the bullet list” in the editor.

nodes.label: Feature bullets · Style the bullet titles

translations.en: Styles the main line of every feature bullet: font, size, weight, color, alignment, and spacing, applied to all bullets at once. Keep bullet titles bold and easy to read so each benefit lands at a glance. The theme defaults usually work, so change them only if a benefit is hard to read.

nodes.label: Feature bullets · Style the bullet icons

translations.en: Styles the small icon or image on each bullet: how it sits in its box (fit shows the whole image, fill crops it to cover), how rounded the corners are, and the spacing around it, applied to all bullets at once. Keep icon size and shape consistent so the checklist looks tidy. The theme defaults are a safe start.
